summary: Since May 2026 most visitors to Chad must apply for an e-Visa on the official platform evisa.td — a visa issued elsewhere after 21 May 2026 is not valid for entry. Citizens of the CEMAC states and of some 15 other countries on the platform's exemption list enter without a visa. Border regions carry serious security risks.

notes: Photography requires care: photographing military sites, government buildings or airports without a permit is illegal.
Export of animal products and cultural artefacts without authorization is prohibited.

payments.text: Cash rules. Cards are accepted only at one or two international hotels in N'Djamena and ATMs are scarce and unreliable. Bring CFA francs or euros to exchange, and carry enough cash for any travel outside the capital.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel to Chad's northern provinces (Borkou, Ennedi Ouest, Ennedi Est and Tibesti), western Kanem, the Lake Chad region (Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa activity) and within 30 km of the other borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country, including N'Djamena. Armed robbery is common in parts of N'Djamena and carjacking a high risk on roads outside it.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Chad travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February brings the coolest, driest conditions — the season for Zakouma National Park and expeditions to the Ennedi massif; from March the heat becomes extreme, and the July–September rains close many routes.

tips.text: Stay away from the Lake Chad basin and the borders with Libya, Sudan and the Central African Republic — these areas see jihadist activity, armed banditry and military operations, and most governments classify them as no-go zones.

Apply only through evisa.td, 7 to 90 days before you travel — Chad's immigration service says visas issued outside the platform after 21 May 2026 are invalid, fees are not refunded and an issued e-Visa cannot be corrected, so check the form before paying.
Register with the immigration authorities (Sûreté Nationale) within 72 hours of arrival — hotels in N'Djamena can usually help, and the stamp is checked when you leave.
Be extremely careful with cameras — photographing military sites, government buildings or airports without a permit is illegal and can lead to arrest.
Zakouma National Park — one of Africa's great conservation revivals — is Chad's standout draw; visits run November to April and are best booked through the park's official operators well in advance.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chad?
faq.answer: Yes, unless your passport is exempt. Chad's e-Visa platform lists Barbados, Benin, the Central African Republic, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Dominica, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Malaysia, Mali, Micronesia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Singapore, Suriname and Togo. Cameroon, a CEMAC member, is not on that list, so Cameroonians should confirm before travel. Everyone else applies online at evisa.td.

faq.question: Does Chad have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is now the only way to get one. Since 11 May 2026 every visa application is made on evisa.td (diplomatic and courtesy visas excepted), and a visa issued outside the platform after 21 May 2026 does not allow entry. Apply at least 7 and no more than 90 days before arrival. A new fee grid has been announced, but the platform does not publish the amounts.

faq.question: Is Chad safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Only partly. The UK advises against all but essential travel to the whole country, including N'Djamena, and against all travel to the Ennedi and Tibesti provinces, the Lake Chad region and within 30 km of the borders. Check current government travel advice before booking.

faq.question: Do I have to register after arriving in Chad?
faq.answer: Yes — foreign visitors are expected to register with the immigration authorities within about 72 hours of arrival. Hotels in N'Djamena can usually arrange it; keep the receipt, as it may be checked on departure.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Chad?
faq.answer: Yes, carry it. Chad's e-Visa platform tells applicants to bring proof of yellow fever vaccination, which immigration checks on arrival.
